text:
anya: Thinking out loud — propose we split the control plane into two explicitly: a thin control-facade (public API, validation, auth) and a control-core (policy engine, orchestration, state). Aim: reduce coupling, shrink blast radius, and make incremental tech-debt paydown feasible. Thoughts?

ji-hoon: +1 on the separation but worried about state ownership. Do we keep the existing config DB as the single source-of-truth? or do we introduce a control-core DB and migrate pieces gradually?

anya: prefer dual-write for a transitional period, with control-facade continuing to accept writes and mirroring to control-core. Then switch reads per-route when safe. Dual-write complexity is the main cost.

marta: sounds reasonable. Phased approach idea: 1) Create control-facade interface and proxy layer; 2) Move stateless flows and validators into facade; 3) Extract heavier orchestration into core; 4) Migrate state with a small, idempotent migration job; 5) Remove legacy paths. Keep each phase <2 weeks.

ji-hoon: agree on phases. A few concerns: sticky session behavior, KV cache ownership (who owns eviction TTLs), and rollout signal (how do we verify parity while both systems serving).

anya: for parity we should have automated contract tests that run in CI and a live "shadow mode" where control-facade forwards to core and compares responses asynchronously. If mismatches exceed threshold -> rollback.

marta: to add — expose a parity dashboard: rate of mismatches, top endpoints, featurization diffs. Also track resource delta (GPU/CPU) because orchestration changes can change autoscaler behavior.

ji-hoon: sticky sessions: propose a shim that honors existing session cookie and routes to the same runtime host until migration cutover. For KV cache, option A: control-core becomes canonical owner and facade is read-through cache; option B: facade owns short-lived in-memory cache and core stores long-term. I prefer A for consistency.

anya: A works if we can keep cache latency under SLO. We'll need a metrics plan: 95p tail, p99 latency of control API, error rate, parity-mismatch rate, and influx of orphaned sessions.

marta: add rollout knobs: per-service feature flag, canary by org, and traffic-splitting 5/95 -> 25/75 -> 100. Also schedule a hard cutoff window and a plan for fast rollback.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: related RFC: https://go/redwood/rfc/control-bisection — PR #3421 opened by @anya.

anya: example proxy config (very small):
```
# facade proxy routes
route /v1/control/* -> facade
facade: validate -> auth -> mirror-write -> proxy-to-core
mirror-write: async POST /internal/mirror
```

ji-hoon: example health-check for parity job:
```
curl -s -X POST https://staging/redwood/internal/compare 
  -d '{"id":"session-123","req":{...}}' | jq .result
# result: {"match":true, "diffs":[]}
```

marta: tickets we should create right away: [ARCH-ctl-001] facade skeleton + proxy, [ARCH-ctl-002] contract-test harness, [ARCH-ctl-003] shadow-mirror infra, [ARCH-ctl-004] migration job + idempotency checks, [ARCH-ctl-005] parity dashboard. Keep tickets small.

anya: ownership: eng-platform gets first two tickets, eng-runtime for orchestration extraction, infra for migration infra. We'll mark eng-ml if any model-serving hooks need rewire.

ji-hoon: one last thing — SLO guardrails in facade code: when core becomes unreachable, we should degrade gracefully (reject new orchestration but allow read-only queries) and emit a distinct error code for clients to handle.

anya: agreed. we'll draft the rollout playbook with rollback steps and emergency toggles. I'll open the first three tickets and the RFC link.

marta: sounds good, please @ji-hoon and @marta on the RFC PR for review. I'll prepare the parity dashboard prototype. :thumbsup:

ji-hoon: will sketch the eviction and TTL proposal tomorrow.

anya: thanks all — let's keep changes small and reversible. :v:
